[api-gateway#Integrations]
ApiGateway: Integrations
ApiGateway calls the OrdersAPI and the UsersAPI. It depends on the user service for token validation, so a request with an expired token is rejected at the edge before any service sees it.

ApiGateway and SearchService share the same on-call rotation, because both sit on the storefront's critical path.

[api-gateway#Overview]
ApiGateway: Overview
ApiGateway fronts every public endpoint. Clients never reach a service directly; every request enters through the gateway, which terminates TLS, applies rate limits per client key, and forwards the request to the owning service.

[api-gateway#Operations]
ApiGateway: Operations
The gateway does not retry failed upstream requests. A 5xx from a service is passed to the client unchanged, and the client library decides whether to retry.

OrdersAPI via ApiGateway -CALLS-> OrdersAPI
OrderService via ApiGateway -CALLS-> OrdersAPI (exposed by OrderService)
UserService via ApiGateway -DEPENDS_ON-> UserService
UsersAPI via ApiGateway -CALLS-> UsersAPI
OrdersPostgresDatabase via OrderService -STORES-> OrdersPostgresDatabase then ApiGateway -CALLS-> OrdersAPI (exposed by OrderService)
PaymentsAPI via OrderService -CALLS-> PaymentsAPI then ApiGateway -CALLS-> OrdersAPI (exposed by OrderService)
PaymentsService via OrderService -CALLS-> PaymentsAPI (exposed by PaymentsService) then ApiGateway -CALLS-> OrdersAPI (exposed by OrderService)
UsersPostgresDatabase via UserService -STORES-> UsersPostgresDatabase then ApiGateway -DEPENDS_ON-> UserService
